_design_note: M4 anchor plus a behaviour-cloned warm start. Two factors change together on purpose: the initial weights, and the exploration start (E07 1.00 -> E08 0.20). They are coupled -- holding epsilon at 1.00 over a cloned policy spends the clone before it can be used -- so this is declared as a two-factor increment rather than pretending to be one. The known bias: rule_based_agent emitted WAIT exactly 0 times in 150,000 recorded loot-crate states, so the clone never waits. The handcrafted line's standing failure is the opposite one (WAIT ranked above a visible escape, docs/05 section 0.13), so wait_fraction and the 'saw the exit and waited' diagnostic count are what to read here, not score. EXPLORATION SCHEDULE: E09, counted in environment steps rather than rounds. The pilot (runs/m4_pilot_20260827) measured why: at epsilon 1.00 a loot-crate round lasts 9.8 steps because random play kills itself at once, and 210 steps once the agent survives. Under E07's 100-round hold the buffer therefore held 982 of the 10,000 transitions min_size requires, and the first gradient step did not land until round 826 -- with epsilon already annealed to 0.11, which is precisely the cold start E07 existed to provide. E09 holds epsilon at 1.00 for 10,000 steps, exactly min_size, so the first gradient step sees a full buffer at full exploration, then anneals over 200,000 steps.

_predeclared_design_numbers.changed_factor: initial_model (none -> behaviour cloning) together with exploration_version (E07 -> E08).
_predeclared_design_numbers.control: The M4 anchor arm at the same budget and seeds.
_predeclared_design_numbers.demonstrations: pretraining/demonstrations/rule_based_agent_loot-crate_v2_150000.npz, sha256 dbf1d002cb5865c36600423ec4f624d9a9412045bf6d2fbea7ce3ed6209eb685: 150000 states over 477 loot-crate rounds. Action counts UP 34282 / RIGHT 34607 / DOWN 34261 / LEFT 34372 / WAIT 0 / BOMB 12478. Cloned for 3 epochs to 0.897 validation accuracy against a 0.231 majority class.
_predeclared_design_numbers.falsification: If the final score is indistinguishable from the anchor's and the early checkpoints are not clearly higher, the warm start bought nothing and is not carried into the final agent.
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction: The early evaluated checkpoints (1000, 2000) exceed the anchor's by more than 4.7. No prediction is made about the final score.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reporting: Quote evaluation_summary.json reportable_result, never selected_checkpoint: the latter maximises over train_seed x checkpoint_round and is biased upward. Report all five training-seed distributions, every G2 threshold, and coins_share alongside score for every arm that has opponents.
_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_loot_crate: docs/01 section 7.21: the five-seed spread of the handcrafted control gives sd 3.77, so two arms measured once each need a gap of 4.7. That threshold covers training variance; the tournament one below does not.
_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_tournament: docs/01 section 7.20: pooled 450-round classic-with-opponents score has sd 0.089, so two arms need a gap of 0.246 (coins_share: 0.022). This was measured by re-running ONE fixed set of checkpoints, so it is evaluation noise only and does NOT cover training variance. Use it for a paired same-seed difference, never to bless a maximum taken over seeds.
_predeclared_design_numbers.selection_protocol: Pool the five training seeds at each checkpoint round; pick the round on the pooled VALIDATION curve; freeze it; then read the holdout numbers at that round. Holdout is never used to decide whether to continue an arm.
